subject: 🏃 Thursday — Steady Base ~55 min (Wk 6)
html:
Tomorrow evening: ~50–55 min easy/steady run from the front door (housekeeper window, after 4:30 PM). Time-capped to fit the solo-parenting constraint — yields ~6–6.5 mi on the hilly home roads. No quality component, no fast finish. Pure aerobic investment.

HR is the governor: ≤145 BPM (easy) / up to 155 BPM (steady). Pace floats with the hills — expect it to slow on the climbs and quicken on the descents. Whatever pace comes out at the right HR is correct. On the descents, shorten your stride and keep the cadence up — the patellofemoral joint doesn't need bombing downhills the day after heavy squats.

Pre-run activation (5 min): quadruped hip CARs (3 each leg), banded lateral walks (10 each direction), glute bridges (10 reps), plus PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

Fatigue check — this is the session to read honestly. Tuesday was a cumulative-fatigue flag (solo parenting + Boston jet lag + post-cold + Sunday's suffer-166 long run), and tonight's heavy strength will add to the legs. If you get out there tomorrow and HR is climbing to 150+ at what feels like a shuffle, that's real information — shorten to 40 min and walk it in. The 14-miler with 5 mi @ MP on Sunday is the session that matters this week. Thursday exists to support it, not compete with it.

Focus cue: let the watch do the thinking. Glance at HR, not pace. If the number is under 145, you're golden — don't speed up just because the pace reads 9:30+. That's the whole point of HR governance on hills.

Context: Week 6 of 12, Phase 2 (Strength & Threshold). Presidio Half Marathon is 10 days out — the Pivot test that gates the 3:30 → 3:25 upgrade. This week's priority is banking volume and protecting Sunday's long run, not chasing intensity. Knee has been 1/5 for every session this week. 45 days to race day.

Lay out your running kit before bed tonight so you're not scrambling when the housekeeper arrives. Hydrate well through the day — you're stacking an evening run on top of an evening lift. Bed by 10.
